questions.q:
Consider the following statements about ancient Bihar:
1. Lord Buddha attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya.
2. Vardhaman Mahavira, founder of Jainism, attained Nirvana at Pawapuri, Bihar.
3. Pataliputra was founded by Ajatashatru's successors as a fortified outpost.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Buddha attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya and Mahavira attained Nirvana at Pawapuri, both correct. Pataliputra's founding is traditionally credited to Ajatashatru himself (as a fort at Patali village), not merely his successors as an 'outpost'.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q: The first mention of the geographical area of Bihar (as Videha) is found in which text?
questions.explanation: The Shatapath Brahmana (composed ~800 BC) gives the first mention of Bihar as 'Videha' (the Tirhut-Mithila region). In the Rigveda Bihar is referred to as Kikat and Vratya.

questions.q: Which of the following Mahajanapadas was NOT spread in the region of present-day Bihar?
questions.explanation: Of the 16 Mahajanapadas, three lay in Bihar — Magadha, Vajji/Lichchhavi and Anga. Kosala was in Uttar Pradesh.

questions.q: Which dynasty is considered to have been founded by Bimbisara in 544 BC and is also called the 'patricide dynasty'?
questions.explanation: The Haryanka dynasty, founded by Bimbisara in 544 BC, is known as the Pitrahanta (patricide) dynasty because rulers were killed by their own sons.

questions.q: Who shifted the capital of Magadha from Rajgriha to Pataliputra?
questions.explanation: Udayan/Udayin, son of Ajatashatru, shifted the capital from Rajgriha to Pataliputra, situated at the confluence of the Ganga, Son and Gandak.

questions.q: The First Buddhist Council was held in which year and at which place?
questions.explanation: The First Buddhist Council was held in 483 BC in the Saptaparni cave of Rajgir under the patronage of Ajatashatru, chaired by Mahakashyap; it compiled the Sutta Pitaka and Vinaya Pitaka.

questions.q: Which ruler organized the Third Buddhist Council at Pataliputra?
questions.explanation: Ashoka organized the Third Buddhist Council at Pataliputra (~250 BC), chaired by Moggaliputta Tissa, where the Abhidhamma Pitaka was compiled.

questions.q: Who established the Nanda dynasty by ending the Shishunaga dynasty, assuming the title 'Ekarat'?
questions.explanation: Mahapadmananda founded the Nanda dynasty in 344 BC and assumed the title 'Ekarat'/'Ekachhatra'. Dhanananda was its last ruler.

questions.q:
Arrange the following dynasties of Magadha in their correct chronological (earliest-first) order:
1. Maurya  2. Nanda  3. Haryanka  4. Shishunaga
questions.explanation: Chronological order: Haryanka (544 BC) → Shishunaga (412 BC) → Nanda (344 BC) → Maurya (321 BC).

questions.q: Which Greek ambassador wrote 'Indica' describing the Mauryan empire?
questions.explanation: Seleucus sent Megasthenes as ambassador to Chandragupta Maurya's court; Megasthenes wrote 'Indica'. Deimachus and Dionysius visited Bindusara's court.

questions.q: In the Kalinga War (261 BC) which Major Rock Edict of Ashoka describes the war?
questions.explanation: The Kalinga War is described in Ashoka's 13th Major Rock Edict. After this war Ashoka embraced Buddhism.

questions.q: Who established Nalanda University during the Gupta period?
questions.explanation: Nalanda University was established during the reign of Kumaragupta I (415-455 AD). It later became the greatest centre of Buddhist education.

questions.q: Who was the founder of the Pala dynasty, and which ruler founded Vikramshila University?
questions.explanation: Gopala founded the Pala dynasty in 750 AD (and Odantapuri University). His son Dharmapala founded Vikramshila University at Bhagalpur.

questions.q: Which ruler destroyed Nalanda and Vikramshila universities and conquered Bihar Sharif (Odantapuri) in 1198 AD?
questions.explanation: Bakhtiyar Khilji, a slave of Qutbuddin Aibak, conquered Odantapuri (Bihar Sharif) in 1198 AD and later set fire to Nalanda and Vikramshila.

questions.q: Who was the founder of the Karnat dynasty of Mithila, with its capital at Simraongarh?
questions.explanation: The Karnat dynasty of Mithila-Tirhut was founded by Nanyadeva, with its capital at Simraongarh (now in Nepal). Harisimhadeva was its last ruler.

questions.q: Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun at which two battles to establish the Sur dynasty?
questions.explanation: Sher Khan defeated Humayun at Chausa in 1539 AD (taking the title Sher Shah) and at Kannauj (Bilgram) in 1540 AD, establishing the Sur dynasty in Delhi.

questions.q: Which silver and copper coins were introduced by Sher Shah Suri?
questions.explanation: Sher Shah Suri introduced the pure silver coin 'Rupiya' and the copper coin 'Dam'.

questions.q: Who rebuilt/fortified Patna and made it the capital of Bihar in 1541 AD?
questions.explanation: In 1541 AD Sher Shah Suri built the fort of Patna and made it the capital of Bihar. Its description is found in Tarikh-i-Dawoodi.

questions.q: The revolt of 1857 in Bihar was mainly led by which person?
questions.explanation: Babu Kunwar Singh, the zamindar of Jagdishpur, led the revolt of 1857 in Bihar. After his death (26 April 1858), his brother Amar Singh continued the struggle.

questions.q: In which year did Gandhiji start the Champaran Satyagraha, his first Satyagraha in India?
questions.explanation: The Champaran Satyagraha (1917) against the exploitative Teenkathiya indigo system was Gandhiji's first Satyagraha in India. He reached Motihari on 15 April 1917.

questions.q: Which leader escaped from Hazaribagh jail on Diwali night (9 Nov 1942) and founded the 'Azad Dasta'?
questions.explanation: Jayaprakash Narayan escaped from Hazaribagh jail on 9 November 1942 with five companions and formed the Azad Dasta during the Quit India Movement.

questions.q: Who was martyred when the Patna Secretariat flag-hoisting procession was fired upon on 11 August 1942 (seven martyrs)? Select the correct statement.

options.A: Seven students were martyred and the eighth, Ram Krishna Singh, finally hoisted the flag
options.D: The firing was ordered by the Governor

questions.answer_text: Seven students were martyred and the eighth, Ram Krishna Singh, finally hoisted the flag
questions.explanation: Seven students (Umakant Sinha, Ramanand Singh, Satish Prasad Jha, Rajendra Singh, Ramgovind Singh, Devipad Chaudhary, Jagpati Kumar) were martyred; the eighth student Ram Krishna Singh succeeded in hoisting the flag on the Secretariat.

questions.q: Which session of the Indian National Congress was held in Gaya (1922), presided over by Chittaranjan Das?
questions.explanation: The 37th session of the Congress was held in 1922 at Gaya, presided over by Deshbandhu Chittaranjan Das. The Swaraj Party was later founded by those favouring entry into legislatures.

questions.q: In the Quit India Movement (1942), the slogan given by Mahatma Gandhi was:
questions.explanation: Gandhiji gave the slogan 'Do or Die' (Karo Ya Maro) at the launch of the Quit India Movement on 8 August 1942.
